issues.legal_issue: A deed creating a charitable endowment that permits benefits without religious, caste, or creed restrictions creates a secular public charitable trust rather than a wakf.
material_facts: The deed authorized the trust property and income to be used for relief of the poor, religious institutions, education, medical relief, and other objects of general public utility.
The deed stated that the charitable benefits were not to be restricted to any particular religion and contemplated purposes without distinction of religion, caste, or creed.
The deed transferred legal title to the trustees and gave them discretion to select and fund the specified charitable purposes.
The deed appointed trustees including non-Muslims and provided for management not restricted by Muslim-law rules.
issues.conclusion: The deed created a secular, comprehensive public charitable trust, not a wakf.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(1) of the Wakf Act, 1954, covers a permanent dedication for purposes recognized by Muslim law as pious, religious, or charitable. The Court distinguished a wakf, in which ownership is transferred to God, from a trust in which legal title is vested in trustees, relying on Vidya Varuthi Thirtha v. Balusami Ayyar, (1921) L.R. 48 I.A. 302. In construing an instrument, where two constructions are reasonably possible, the construction that gives effect to all its clauses is preferred to one that defeats some clauses.

rule.if: charitable_endowment_classification_case and unrestricted_public_charitable_purposes and legal_title_vested_in_trustees and broad_trustee_discretion

predicates.charitable_endowment_classification_case: The proceeding requires classification of an instrument that creates a charitable endowment.
predicates.unrestricted_public_charitable_purposes: The instrument permits charitable benefits without restriction to a particular religion, caste, or creed.
predicates.legal_title_vested_in_trustees: The instrument transfers legal title to the endowment property to trustees.
predicates.broad_trustee_discretion: The instrument gives trustees broad discretion to select and fund its charitable purposes.

issues.definition: When a charitable-endowment classification proceeding concerns an instrument with unrestricted public charitable purposes, title vested in trustees, and broad trustee discretion, the rule treats the endowment as a secular public charitable trust rather than a wakf.

issues.legal_issue: Registration under a statutory scheme for wakfs is invalid when the endowment being registered is not a wakf within the scheme's definition.
material_facts: The Wakf Board treated the trust as a wakf and caused it to be registered after the trustees did not comply with its request to register it.
The deed created a secular public charitable trust rather than a wakf.
The registration was made under section 28 of the Wakf Act, 1954.
issues.conclusion: The trust's registration under section 28 was invalid and inoperative because the trust was not a wakf.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3(1) and 28 of the Wakf Act, 1954, apply to wakfs within the statutory definition; a trust outside that definition cannot validly be registered under the Act. The Court relied on its construction of the trust deed and the distinction between a wakf and a secular charitable trust discussed in Vidya Varuthi Thirtha v. Balusami Ayyar, (1921) L.R. 48 I.A. 302.

predicates.endowment_registration_validity_case: The proceeding challenges the registration of an endowment under a statutory scheme for wakfs.
predicates.endowment_falls_outside_wakf_definition: The endowment is not a permanent dedication for purposes recognized by Muslim law as pious, religious, or charitable.

issues.definition: When a proceeding challenges statutory wakf registration and the endowment falls outside the wakf definition, the rule treats the registration as invalid and inoperative.
